picks.editorial_note: RWTH Aachen's HydroGym, published in Nature, is a genuine research breakthrough: an open-source reinforcement-learning platform that lets AI agents actively control fluid dynamics, with direct applications in energy, transportation, and defense systems.
picks.title: Training AI Agents that Can Actively Control Fluid Dynamics in Energy, Transportation, and Defense | RWTH Aachen University | EN

picks.editorial_note: Imperial College London and Thomson Reuters built a $40M frontier AI model by fine-tuning an open-source base, demonstrating a technically novel and far cheaper path to 'sovereign AI' that could reshape how nations and industries build independent AI capacity.
picks.title: Imperial and Thomson Reuters pioneer new technical approach that could broaden access to sovereign AI

picks.editorial_note: EPFL's framework teaching LLMs to express calibrated uncertainty ('doubt') when proposing experiments is a meaningful methodological advance for AI-driven scientific discovery, addressing a core reliability problem in using AI as a research collaborator.
picks.title: An AI capable of doubt can optimize scientific discovery

picks.editorial_note: UT Austin's fusion seed grants tie into DOE's new Genesis Mission, a major federal initiative applying AI to accelerate fusion energy research — signaling significant government investment at the intersection of AI and energy security.
picks.title: Fusion Energy Seed Grants Launch New Interdisciplinary Collaborations at UT Austin - UT News
picks.university: The University of Texas at Austin

picks.editorial_note: A $2.88M DOE award to a University of Houston-led coalition targets AI-driven discovery of critical-mineral alternatives, directly addressing U.S. supply-chain vulnerabilities tied to foreign-controlled rare-earth sources.
picks.title: Department of Energy Awards UH-led Team $2.88M to Use AI to Strengthen America’s Critical Mineral Supply Chain | University of Houston

picks.editorial_note: A $7.7M federal partnership between University of Kansas engineers, the Army Corps of Engineers, and DHS is applying AI-integrated digital twins to inspect and strengthen aging American dams — critical infrastructure with real public-safety stakes.
picks.title: Four years later KU researchers continue their work strengthening American dams

picks.editorial_note: A $40M Department of Labor grant led by Jobs for the Future, with University of Cincinnati as a partner, will expand AI and semiconductor apprenticeships — a large-scale federal bet on building the AI-era skilled workforce.
picks.title: Major grant expands apprenticeship opportunities at UC

picks.editorial_note: Kent State's DOE Genesis Mission-funded project to mine 50 years of water-chemistry data into a continental-scale AI framework shows the federal initiative's reach extending into environmental and natural-resource science.
picks.title: Streams Never Lie; Kent State Magazine; Fall 2026

picks.editorial_note: UNSW Canberra's new large-scale indoor robotics and drone testing arena, one of Australia's biggest, expands the country's autonomous-systems research infrastructure and deepens ties between academia and defense/industry partners.
picks.title: New facilities expand innovation ecosystem at UNSW Canberra City

picks.editorial_note: NJIT's selection as one of just 14 U.S. institutions for NSF's new CyberAI Scholarships-for-Service program reflects a federal policy push to build a pipeline of talent at the AI-cybersecurity intersection.
picks.title: Federal Scholarships Now Available Where AI and Cybersecurity Meet
